result.summary: The street environment is characterized by a lack of continuous pedestrian infrastructure, with a narrow sidewalk present only on one side. The presence of large parked vehicles and blank industrial frontages creates a low-visibility, uninviting environment for walking.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk
hazards.description: The left side of the street lacks a paved walkway, forcing pedestrians to walk on an unpaved shoulder or in the roadway.

hazards.name: Narrow and Obstructed Sidewalk
hazards.description: The existing sidewalk on the right is very narrow and obstructed by a traffic cone and utility poles.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked trucks and vehicles block sightlines between pedestrians and moving traffic.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Install a continuous, ADA-compliant sidewalk on the left side of the street to provide a safe walking path.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Widen the existing sidewalk on the right to meet minimum accessibility standards and clear obstructions.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the nearest intersection to improve visibility and reduce crossing distances.

result.summary: The street features a continuous concrete sidewalk directly adjacent to residential row houses, but lacks a buffer from the roadway. A large parked van creates a significant visual obstruction for pedestrians, and the environment lacks safety enhancements like lighting, trees, or traffic calming.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicle
hazards.description: A large black van parked at the curb significantly blocks sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and any approaching traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground right, parked along the curb

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is immediately adjacent to the travel lane with no physical buffer like trees or a furniture zone to protect pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the entire visible curb line

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Install street trees or a planting buffer between the sidewalk and the curb to provide physical separation and improve the pedestrian environment.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add street lighting to improve visibility and safety for pedestrians during evening hours, as no luminaires are currently visible.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is constrained by narrow sidewalks that are further obstructed by utility poles, particularly on the left side of the street. High levels of on-street parking on both sides of the narrow roadway create visual obstructions and limit the space available for safe pedestrian movement.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located directly in the center of the narrow sidewalk on the left, forcing pedestrians into the roadway or against building walls.

hazards.name: Substandard Sidewalk Width
hazards.description: The sidewalks on both sides are extremely narrow, making it difficult for two people to pass or for those with mobility aids to navigate.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of a narrow street limits sightlines between pedestrians attempting to cross and oncoming drivers.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Reallocate a portion of the roadway or parking lane to widen the sidewalks, ensuring a clear, unobstructed path of travel that meets accessibility standards.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to narrow the roadway at crossing points, which improves visibility and reduces the distance pedestrians must spend in the street.

interventions.title: Utility Pole Relocation or Undergrounding
interventions.description: Relocate utility poles to the furniture zone or underground the lines to remove physical barriers from the pedestrian clear zone.

result.summary: The image shows a very restricted view of a street environment, dominated by a large parked truck that creates a significant visual obstruction. No pedestrian infrastructure, such as sidewalks or crossings, is visible, making it impossible to fully assess the safety of the built environment.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A large truck is parked close to the building, completely blocking sightlines between the building frontage and the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image, blocking the lower half of the building and the street level.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking near building entrances and potential crossing points to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Ensure a continuous, unobstructed sidewalk is provided to separate pedestrians from vehicle traffic and parking areas.
